| **ADR-471** | 2026-10-11 | Sync / task 2.6.2 cut in four; a sync, the idempotency ledger and a held record as tables with their own guards *(task 2.6.2, part 1 of 4; three migrations, no endpoint, no dependency; agent defaults; amends ADR-468 (3)'s last sentence; ARCHITECTURE §5, §9 (1), (3), (4), §10; `spec/DATA-MODEL.md` §4.5; ADR-022, 097, 100, 113, 336, 401, 438, 440, 467…470; AC-05-04, 16, 46, AC-06-58; C53, C69, C70, C128; REQ-016, 203)* | **What the standards ask of this layer, said before building (ADR-401; by chapter, the numbered requirements are 2.7.3's):** ASVS V16 (security logging), a log entry says who, what and when with a time that can be trusted, and can't be changed or removed afterwards: a sync keeps both clocks and their difference and nobody edits or deletes one; ASVS V2 and API Security Top 10's API4 (unrestricted resource consumption), what a client may make the server keep is bounded: the same thing sent again is the same held record, without relying on a per-phone limit (ADR-468 (4)); API1 and API5 (authorisation at the object and at the function), a row is written only for the phone that proved itself and only by the service whose work it is, enforced by the database too (ARCHITECTURE §5). Part 3: what the answer carries besides the answers (fresh lists, a new passcode check, the setup version sent) and the worker reading the clock's difference for `DEVICE_CLOCK_OFF`, its threshold a policy value (C53, C70). Part 4: the harness's phones through it in place of `SyncStandIn`, their reports and numbers in the sync (C130). **(2) `Sync`** (table `sync`): the phone, `startedAt` (the server's clock), `deviceClockAt` with `deviceUtcOffsetMinutes` beside it (as every time a phone reports has; DATA-MODEL listed no offset), `clockDifferenceSeconds` and `setupVersionSent`. **The difference is the phone's clock less the server's, in whole seconds, above nought when the phone's is ahead**; the database holds it to the two instants (within a second, so the rounding is the service's to pick), and it is a `bigint`, since the contract takes any instant and a clock at year 9999 is past an `int`. Nothing of a sync changes after it is written but `setupVersionSent`, written once. **(3) `SyncedRecord`, the ledger** (table `synced_record`): one row for each record the server **stored**, as a record of its kind (`SAVED`) or in quarantine (`QUARANTINED`), keyed on the phone-made id, with its kind (the contract's word, text held to that form, so a later kind needs no migration), its sync and its phone (held to the sync's by a two-column foreign key). What was sent is never changed and never deleted. **The audit log says that a held record was made and never holds a second copy of what was sent** (`payload` is named on its audit trigger): the row itself can't be changed, so nothing is lost, and up to a mebibyte of what may name a private citizen is not doubled. Only a permitted person in the back office changes it, in place and audited (ADR-051), once the server has it. **(2) Before submitting** a record is open and its monitor's to adjust, for days where the work takes days; nothing flags it for having stood open (no flag does today; the times it records are still checked as any are, ADR-100). **(3) Overturned:** ADR-072 ("reopened until it syncs", with the device's change log) and ADR-240 (6) ("reopenable until the monitor ends the shift", an agent default, with the edit log); ARCHITECTURE §9 step 8 and its ADR-240 note are struck with a note. **(4) Withdrawn:** task 2.6.3 and ADR-476. The table `field_event_edit`, its two migrations, its tests and its list entries were removed from the working folder the same day, uncommitted; the local installation, which held only its seed (3 actors, no project, phone or record), was re-made by `pnpm installer:teardown` and a first run to take the two applied migrations back out, as on 2026-10-07 (ADR-401). `FieldEventEdit` leaves `spec/DATA-MODEL.md`. **(5) What the server owes the rule is already built** (ADR-472): a record sent again under its id is answered "already saved" from the ledger and nothing is tried, so no phone, tampered with or not, changes a record the server has. Now proven by name: `apps/api/test/sync.test.ts`, a disposal at 85% sent again at 95% is answered `ALREADY_SAVED`, the field event, its audit records and the queue as they were, nothing held. | **ADR-480** | 2026-10-12 | Media / the store and the API's identity at it *(task 2.6.4, part 1 of 5; ARCHITECTURE §4 "Backups", §6 "Uploads", §11; `spec/THREAT-MODEL.md` T-25, A4; ADR-098, 101, 263, 264, 455, 479; AC-10-49 in part; BACKLOG C24; no migration, no endpoint; agent defaults, marked)* | **What the standards ask of this layer, said before building (ADR-401):** ASVS V5 (file handling: stored outside the web root, never run, the name never a caller's), V13 (configuration: least privilege for every service identity, secrets out of code and logs), V16 (errors that tell a caller nothing of the inside); API Security Top 10 API7 (a request the server makes is to a server the settings name, never one a caller chose) and API10 (an answer from another program is checked). **(1) One bucket, one identity, the least it can be.** The local stack's object store gains a second identity, `open-adms-api`, beside its administrator: its one policy (`open-adms-media-write-once`, in `infra/local/compose.yaml`) allows `s3:PutObject` and `s3:GetObject` on the media bucket's objects and nothing else. **Seen at the store itself:** it can delete no object (one, a version by its id, or several at once), delete no bucket, make no bucket, list no bucket's objects or versions, is shown no bucket when it asks which exist, can change no bucket's versioning or policy, and can put nothing in any other bucket (C24, ADR-263). (2) **The bucket is `adms-media`**, made by `pnpm local:up` through the store's own shell and never by the API, and it **keeps every version** (ARCHITECTURE §4): `up` stops if it doesn't. `up` also adds the identity's two halves to an `infra/local/.env` made before them (every line already there left as it was) and makes the store's container afresh where it doesn't know the identity yet. (3) **`MediaStore`** (`apps/api/src/media/media-store.ts`; `Media` is what a test hands in its place): `keep(key, bytes, type)` puts **only where nothing is kept under the key** (`If-None-Match: *`) and answers `KEPT` or `ALREADY_THERE`, the first file standing; `sizeOf(key)`; `read(key, bytesAtMost)`, the bytes as stored with the type they were kept under, refused where larger than the caller will take. **It has no call that deletes, moves, copies or lists.** A key is held to its form before anything is asked (lower-case segments, no empty one, none beginning with a dot, 512 characters); a type is a bare media type. HTTPS only, the certificate checked against the settings' authority or the machine's own; inside the stack the proxy's address is connected to under the store's own name. **An error says what was asked and the store's status or its error's name, never the key, the bucket, the identity or the store's own words.** (4) **Settings** (`Settings.media`): `ADMS_MEDIA_URL`, `ADMS_MEDIA_BUCKET`, `ADMS_MEDIA_REGION`, `ADMS_MEDIA_ACCESS_KEY`, `ADMS_MEDIA_SECRET_KEY`, all five required (a missing or malformed one stops the start by name, AC-10-55); `ADMS_MEDIA_CA_FILE` and `ADMS_MEDIA_ADDRESS` where the installation has them. The installer writes them into `apps/api/.env` from the stack's own (`installer:check` gains a line, 31), and an installation made before them needs `pnpm installer --yes` once. (5) **A policy value, `MEDIA_STORE_ANSWER_SECONDS` = 30**: one question of the store, whole. (6) **Agent defaults, the user's to overturn:** (a) the API's identity may not even list; (b) the bucket's name and the region `us-east-1` for the local store (a firm's own store names its own); (c) the bucket in the path (`forcePathStyle`), the one form every store takes; (d) thirty seconds. SeaweedFS 4.47 refuses every put under a policy that denies one without `If-None-Match` (tried on a throw-away container), so that guard is the code's and the versions are the backstop; **a firm's own store can do more (a deny on unconditional puts, Object Lock), which is the deploy's to set (Phase 5a).** (8) **Not built here:** nothing calls `MediaStore` yet: it is handed to the process with the media endpoint (part 3). **Seen:** `apps/api/test/media-store.test.ts` (8 tests, on the stack's own store over HTTPS; a test's objects are taken away again by the administrator), `door.test.ts` (the API's own container reaches the store under its identity at the proxy's address), `settings.test.ts`; 35 loosenings listed, one slipped (a store key of any length: a case added, then caught), 34 caught at the end; the policy loosened to let the API delete an object failed the identity's test. | The API's identity at the object store may put and get an object in the media bucket and nothing else, and a test holds it to that. `MediaStore` never overwrites, deletes or lists; a file's place is held to its form where the request is made. The media bucket keeps every version. |
| **ADR-481** | 2026-10-12 | Sync / a photograph's record in the sync contract *(task 2.6.4, part 2 of 5; BACKLOG 2.6.4, C24, C65, C82, C127, C129, C130, C134, C135, C136; ARCHITECTURE §9 (2), (3), (4), §11; `spec/THREAT-MODEL.md` T-25; ADR-022, 101, 179, 292, 326, 466…472, 475, 477, 478, 480; AC-04-77, AC-05-05, AC-05-09 in part; one migration; agent defaults, marked)* | **What the standards ask, said before building (ADR-401):** ASVS V5 (a stored file's name is never a caller's), V16 (a log names no record); API Security Top 10 API3 (an answer carries nothing the caller doesn't need: never where a file is kept), API4 (every part of a request bounded). **(1) A photograph's record is a part of a sync of its own, `photos`, read after the records** (`syncedPhotoSchema` in `sync-records.ts`, `photoRead`, `photoNames`, `photoAnswerSchema` and `syncPhotosAtMost` in `sync.ts`): **at most 200 a sync** (agent default; 200 records and 200 photographs' records are under 640 KiB of the request's mebibyte), each read on its own as a record is, each answered in its own place under its id: `SAVED` (with its notes), `ALREADY_SAVED` or `NOT_SAVED`, **never `QUARANTINED`** (a photograph holds no number). `syncAnswerRead` holds the photographs' answers to their places; `syncClientSuite` sends them in two checks (every part sent, empty where there is nothing; each sent once as taken). A photograph is sent in the sync that carries its record or a later one. (2) **What the record says, and nothing else:** its id, its project, what it is of (`owner`: one of seven kinds a phone makes, by that record's id), which of a certification's five views it is (none on any other photograph's: a refine says so before the database does), who took it, when (an instant and its offset) and where (whatever fix the phone had), **both fingerprints as SHA-256 in lower-case hex, the phone's word, written once** (the database's `photo_refuse_file_edit` already holds them), and **whether a depth file goes beside it** (`depthFile`, agent default). **Never where its file is kept, never the file, never an upload's time, never which phone** (strict: such a field makes it no record). (3) **The server makes the place** (`apps/api/src/media/photo-places.ts`, agent default): `projects/<project>/photos/<photograph>`, the depth file at the same place with `.depth` after it, both UUIDs in lower case, so every place passes `MediaStore`'s own form (`isMediaKey`, now exported) and no two photographs share one; a project's files share a prefix, to be moved to a cheaper tier or gathered for a client package a project at a time. Written once with the record, never told to the phone (part 3's endpoint takes a file by the photograph's id). (4) **A photograph whose record the server doesn't have saved is not tried** (agent default): held for a person with a new reason, **`OWNER_NOT_SAVED`** ("Not saved: the record this photograph belongs to isn’t saved on the server. Held on the server for review."; the domain's `NotSaved.ownerNotSaved`, the enum `not_saved_reason` gains the value: migration `20261012213617_a_photograph_whose_record_is_not_saved`). That covers a record held in the same sync or an earlier one, one never sent, and one of another kind than the photograph says. **Sent again once its record is saved, it is saved**; the held row stays for a person to close (Phase 4's queue shows one whose `sentId` was since saved, C132). A record kept in quarantine is a record the server has: its photograph belongs to the quarantined record, as ADR-292 (5) said. What it names that the server doesn't have otherwise (its project, who took it, a record of another project) is the database's refusal, answered `NAMES_NO_RECORD` and held. (5) **Saved, it joins the idempotency ledger** (`recordKind` `PHOTO`: a retry is answered `ALREADY_SAVED` from it) **and queues what reads it:** a field event's photograph its ticket (a pay item may require photographs, ADR-157); a certification's a job naming no ticket, for its views (ADR-179); any other's nothing. `uploadedAt` stays empty until part 3. The sync's log line counts the photographs' answers, never an id. **Nothing a phone sends changes a photograph the server has** (ADR-477): one sent again with other fingerprints is answered `ALREADY_SAVED` and nothing is written. (6) **The by-hand path is gone (C134):** `SentPhoto` is the contract's shape with the phone's id (the hand-written interface with its `objectKey` went), `PhoneRecord` no longer carries a photograph, `PhoneServer.receive` and the phone's by-hand photograph loop went, and so did `P1Syncs.crewPhotographs`: **the harness's phone sends its photographs in its syncs, after their records; Jo's phone in `p1-field-days` photographs each unit rate ticket as she completes it; a certification is sent with its five, by the phone's `certify` and by the P1 stories' `certifyP1` (`photographed`)**, so `CERTIFICATION_PHOTO_MISSING` stands on no story's certification (`p1-reconciled` now holds none, and 25 photographs of a view). `held-for-review` tells a refused certification's five photographs held with it. (7) **Not built here:** no file is sent (the media endpoint is part 3, the stories' files part 4, the map's part 5); a depth file's own fingerprint has no column (part 3 decides whether its check needs one); a phone that sends an upper-case UUID is given a lower-case place (not tried by a test). **Seen:** 150 files and 2,708 tests; 20 stories (`certification` 29 checks); `apps/api/test/sync.test.ts` three tests, `packages/contracts/test/sync.test.ts` three; twenty loosenings caught of twenty. | A phone sends a photograph's record after the records, with both fingerprints and never a place; the server makes the place, holds one whose record it doesn't have saved, and answers the rest saved or already saved, never quarantined. |
| **ADR-482** | 2026-10-12 | Sync / the media endpoint: a photograph's files taken in parts, checked, and kept or set aside *(task 2.6.4, part 3 of 5; BACKLOG 2.6.4, C24, C84 (12), C86, C136, C137; ARCHITECTURE §6 "Uploads", §9 (2), (5), §11; `spec/THREAT-MODEL.md` T-25; ADR-101, 263, 401, 416, 440, 477, 478, 480, 481; AC-04-77, AC-05-09, AC-10-47, AC-10-48 in part, AC-10-49; REQ-203; three migrations; agent defaults, marked)* | **What the standards ask, said before building (ADR-401):** OWASP ASVS 5.0 V5 (a file's size bounded before it is read whole; its kind told by its own content, never by a name or a type it is sent with; stored outside anything served as a page and never run; its name never the caller's), V13 (every service identity the least it can be), V16 (a log says nothing a file holds); API Security Top 10 API4 (every request bounded: a part's size, a file's size, how many parts a phone sends) and API3 (an answer never says where a file is kept); resumable uploads as the tus protocol's core (tus.io 1.0: a part goes at the offset the last one ended at; the server says where it stands). **(1) The media endpoint, the one endpoint that takes a file (AC-10-47):** `GET` and `PATCH /phones/current/photos/:photoId/files/:file` (`photoFileEndpoint`, `sendPhotoFilePartEndpoint`), `file` `photo` or `depth`, `PROVEN_PHONE`, nobody signed in. A part is the body as bytes of `application/offset+octet-stream` (tus's word), with `offset` and the whole file's `length` in the query; the contract marks the one endpoint `file: true` (no body schema, never a `GET`; `taken` reads bytes, at least one; OpenAPI describes it as bytes). **The answer, one shape for both:** `KEPT` (whole, the one fingerprinted, kept: nothing more to send, and a part sent again changes nothing), `RECEIVING` with `received` and `length` (send the rest from `received`; none held is `0` and `null`), `NOT_MATCHED`. Never a place. **No dependency:** a tus server keeps a file's unfinished parts on a disk or as further objects it deletes afterwards, and the API's identity deletes nothing (ADR-480). **(2) Resumable, and what is held meanwhile (agent default):** a part is taken only where it starts the file or goes on where the last ended, inside the file's length; any other is answered with where the file stands, and nothing changes. **The parts of a file not yet whole are held in the API's own memory (`Receiving`), bounded by `MEDIA_RECEIVING_BYTES_AT_MOST` (256 MiB) across every phone; past it the file whose last part came longest ago is let go**, never the one just taken, and its phone is told none is held and starts it again. Nothing unfinished is written to a disk or the store, so the store's identity is widened by nothing: a whole file is one put, as before. The phone keeps every file until it is told `KEPT`, so a restart, or another API process, costs a re-send and loses nothing (Phase 5a: several processes each hold their own). **(3) Checked before anything is held or kept:** the file's `length` at most `MEDIA_FILE_BYTES_AT_MOST` (32 MiB, 413 `TOO_LARGE`); a part at most `MEDIA_PART_BYTES_AT_MOST` (4 MiB), **the media route's own body limit, refused before it is read whole** (413; every other route keeps `REQUEST_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES`); a part never past the file's length (400); **the first part's first 12 bytes an image, by the domain's `photoFileTypeOf`: JPEG, HEIC or HEIF, PNG, TIFF** (agent default, measured on real phones in Phase 3; anything else 415 `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, never held, never stored). The type it is kept under is what its bytes say. **(4) Whole, its SHA-256 is read before it is kept:** the record's `uploadedSha256` (the depth file's `depthSha256`) and **it is kept once, at the place the server made, never overwritten**, and its upload time written (`uploadedAt`, `depthUploadedAt`), **under the device key's actor for that phone** (the phone's own act, nobody signed in, as a proof is, ADR-440). Where something is already at the place (a piece of work that stopped between keeping the file and writing the time), it is read back and its fingerprint checked before the upload is called done; anything else there is the server's failure (500), never kept over (C136). **(5) A file that isn't the one fingerprinted (C84 (12), decided under the shot-clock rule): set aside, never turned away and never kept as the photograph's.** It is a photograph's evidence all the same, or the sign of one swapped (T-25): kept at a place of its own beside the photograph's, `<place>.set-aside/<its SHA-256>`, with a row of the new table `set_aside_file` saying what arrived as the server read it (which file, the phone, its fingerprint, size and type, its place, when); the same file again is one row. The phone is told `NOT_MATCHED` and sends its file again from the first byte; nothing is at the photograph's place until the right one comes. A file that fails its kind or size is refused, never stored (AC-10-47: checked before it is stored). **(6) The depth file's own fingerprint (ADR-481 (7)):** the contract's `depthFile` is replaced by **`depthSha256`** (nullable; a depth file goes beside the photograph exactly where its fingerprint is given), the phone's word, written once, in the new column `photo.depth_sha256`; `photo.depth_uploaded_at` beside it. **(7) The database enforces it** (migrations `20261012230320_a_photographs_files_uploaded`, its guard `…230425_guard_a_photographs_files_uploaded`, and `…230738_guard_a_contractor_user_sees_its_photographs_again`): the depth fingerprint a SHA-256, there exactly where a depth file is, never changed (`photo_depth_check`, `photo_refuse_depth_fingerprint_edit`); **a record is kept before its files reach storage, an upload time is written once, and only with the source `DEVICE` and the photograph's own phone stated** (`photo_upload_guard`); `set_aside_file` the API's alone to add and read, never changed or deleted, audited, its check (`set_aside_file_received_check`), written only for the phone that took its photograph (`set_aside_file_from_its_phone_guard`); no viewer reads it. **A slip of the agent's own:** the guard's rerun of `guard_viewer` on `photo` left out the `own` that ADR-361 gave it, so a contractor user lost its own tickets' photographs; the tests caught it before anything was committed, but the guard was already applied to `adms`, and an applied migration is never edited (ADR-113), so a third migration puts the `own` back. **(8) A phone's parts are a limit of their own:** `FILE_PARTS_BY_PHONE`, `RATE_LIMIT_FILE_PARTS_PER_PHONE` = 300 in the rate limits' stretch (60 s), each question and each part counted for the phone (429 `LIMITED` with how long to wait). **(9) `MediaStore` is handed to the process** (`ProcessParts.media`, `apiMedia`; built from `Settings.media` and `MEDIA_STORE_ANSWER_SECONDS`, closed when the process stops). (2) **`OfficeBrowser`** (`packages/scenarios/src/office-browser.ts`): a person at their browser. **Signed in as a real person is:** email address, password and, where they have one, the code their authenticator shows now (`OneTimeCodes`, the API's own); a password an admin set is changed at once for one of their own (`/password-changes`); an admin or a manager/analyst with no authenticator sets one up at once (`/two-step/setups` and its confirmation). **The session is the cookies the answers set** (`OverHttps`' answer now carries its `set-cookie` lines, `Asked.setCookies`); the CSRF value of each session answer goes with every call past a GET. **The story's clock moves by hours and days:** answered `NOT_SIGNED_IN`, the browser takes a new access token with its refresh token, and where the session has ended (thirty minutes quiet, twelve hours old) the person signs in again with the next code; the request is sent once more. `asked` answers any answer as it came (for a refusal a story checks); `answered` reads a 200 by the endpoint's answer schema and stops the story on anything else, naming the endpoint, the status and the code. (4) **`p1-viewed` through the endpoints:** Dana signs in; she creates the six viewers at `createPerson` and gives each its projects at `setViewerProjects` (14:00); at 14:30 she sets each one's first password, and each signs in and sets their own; **every read is the viewer's request at `/viewer/…`**: the projects, a page of tickets by workflow, a ticket (one not shown is answered **404 `NOT_FOUND`**, as one nobody has, AC-10-29), the ROEs; P1 taken from Summit's user at `setViewerProjects`. **AC-10-30's "nobody reads nothing" is now the door's:** a browser nobody signed in at is answered 401 `NOT_SIGNED_IN` on each of the four reads, and Dana 403 `NOT_ALLOWED` (an admin is no viewer), where the service called in process answered an id with no login and an admin with nothing; the contractor user given no project still reads nothing. **15 checks, as before.** The ROE stays written by hand (no service makes one, ADR-432). **`story.viewed`, the read-only login's client, is gone from the context:** no story reads it now. ### Moved from NEXT.md, 2026-10-02 (ADR-307)

Word for word, so `NEXT.md` keeps only what is live. From its Phase 0 sections:

## Phase 0: Foundation — ✅ done 2026-10-01 *(ADR-093, ADR-103; kept as the record)*

**Why this phase exists.** On 2026-09-25 the user decided:
- **security comes first**, at every layer;
- the plan (skills, spec, ADRs) is the core;
- the code in `database/` is **historical**: early scaffolding, not a base;
- the reconciliation engine is **rebuilt 100%**;
- the platform is **TypeScript end to end with Prisma** (ADR-094).

Build 1's first lesson was "we never designed" (`spec/FROM-BUILD-1.md` §14). Phase 0 designs the
foundation, proves the security-critical pieces, and only then opens the rebuild.

**Objective.** An approved `spec/ARCHITECTURE.md`, answered foundation questions, and a scaffolded
repository in which the database hardening and the scenario harness are proven by tests.

**Scope boundary.**
- **Until ARCHITECTURE sections are approved:** `spec/` and `agent_store/` only (docs).
- **After approval:** the approved layout (`apps/`, `packages/`, `infra/`, `tools/`,
  ARCHITECTURE §18) opens piece by piece, each recorded as an ADR.
- `database/` is **read-only history** (guard hook).
- `api/`, `field-webapp/`, `back-office-webapp/` are empty placeholders, replaced by the approved
  layout.

**Environment.** Decided when §3 is approved and pinned by ADR: Node LTS, Postgres, Prisma,
TypeScript. Docker for the local stack.

a field event has `invoiceLocks` and `qcMarks`): ask for the lock in force with `where: { unlockedAt: null }`, as the worker's `lockedAsInvoiced` does. **A batch**: `projectId`, `name` (once per project, refused as unique), `createdById`. **An acceptance**: `projectId`, `flagId` (once), `reasonId`, `acceptedById`, `acceptedAt`. **A void**: `projectId`, `workflow`, `ticketNumber`, `reasonId`, `voidedById`, `voidedAt`; the unvoid is an update (`liftedById` and `liftedAt` together, `liftNote`), then the row is fixed; one void in force for a ticket. **The database doesn't hold** that only a QC Approved record locks (1.8.5), that a reason is offered for its use (`Reason.uses`; 1.8.4), or a permission (08 point 1; 1.8.3). **What a mark is on, who made it and when can't be updated** (`refuse_edit()`: "Open ADMS never edits a invoice_lock row: a change is a new version"), by any login: a test that needs other values writes another. **A test writes marks** with `qcLike`, `lockLike`, `acceptanceLike`, `voidLike`, `flagOn101001` and `luis()` in `packages/db/test/marks.test.ts`, as the API's login for the person (`actingAs`); an older test's lock states `project_id`. **A new mark table:** `SELECT guard_table('<table>', 'MARK', '<domain>');`, its checks, `guard_viewer('<table>', 'PROJECT'[, own])`, a row in `test/support/viewers.ts`, `domains` and the trigger and check lists in `catalog.test.ts`, `tableGrants` in `grants.test.ts`. **A rerun of `guard_viewer` on `invoice_lock` or `invoice_batch` repeats its `hidden` and `own`** (copy the line from the seventy-sixth migration). **Loosened guards go faster on a part of the tests:** the nine files that hold a table's guards (its own test, `catalog`, `grants`, `transactions`, `transaction-delete`, `viewers`, `guard-table`, `audit`, `no-delete`) took about a minute and a half a copy, two at a time; a loosening caught by part is caught by the whole. What it leaves: BACKLOG C78.

never `@default(now())`, which Prisma's client fills with the app's clock (KD-68).

**People and viewers** (ADR-315): the example world has three read-only viewers
(`world.clientViewer`, given P1; `world.auditor`, given P1 and P2; `world.coastlineViewer`, a
contractor user, given P1); a test issues another with `viewerLike(name, kind, contractor?)` and
`given(viewer, project)`, and states who is looking with `db.viewer(id)`
(`packages/db/test/support/`). **A new table a client user or an auditor should see** gets
`SELECT guard_viewer('<table>', '<PROJECT|PART_OF|NAMED_BY|FIRM>'[, relation, column][, hidden]);`
in its guard migration and a row in `test/support/viewers.ts`; one nobody should see goes in that
file's `unseenTables`; a viewed table that gains a column reruns `guard_viewer` (C59). A
permission or a viewer's project is taken away by archiving, never deleted.

**Rules** (ADR-313): the example world's P1 has the golden mission's first rule in full
(`world.rule`: its id, its two criteria, its action); a test writes more with `ruleLike`,
`criterionLike`, `pickLike` and `actionLike` (`packages/db/test/support/example-world.ts`). A rule
repeats its form's `document_type`; a criterion line its rule's project and form; a pick its line's
project, form and criterion; an action its rule's project. The domain's `ProjectRules.check(rule,
changedFrom)` is what a setup service calls before it saves a rule (1.1.11); `PaysWhen.rules(…)`
returns the rules a pay item keeps, and matching them to the ones already saved is that service's.

**Sites and the map** (ADR-310, 311): the example world's P1 has Marsh Road TDSR (`world.site`)
and Bayline County Landfill (`world.landfill`) in full, with `world.siteTypes`; a test writes
another with `siteLike(world, siteTypeId, …)`, a TDSR/DMS one stating `site_type_key: 'TDSR'`; both
stories write them through `setUpP1Sites` (`packages/scenarios/src/stories/p1.ts`). A site's
tipping fee pay items are `DisposalSiteTippingFee` rows. **`btree_gist` lives in the schema
`extensions`**, which no runtime login may use; Prisma's shadow database drops it before each
replay (`prisma.config.js`, `initShadowDb`), so `prisma migrate dev` works as before.

**Pay items** (ADR-309): the example world's P1 has six of the golden mission's pay items with
Coastline's rates (`world.payItems`, `world.rates`, `world.payableTypes`, `world.kindsOfWork`); a
test enters another with `payItemLike(world, …)` and `insertOf`, since no capture setting has a
database default. An assignment's pay item repeats its `kindOfWorkId`.

**Forms** (ADR-308): a row that belongs only on some kinds of form (`FormDebrisType` on a load or
haul-out form, `FormDefinition` on an ROE, survey, incident or drop-off log form) repeats its form's
`documentType`, held by a check and a two-column foreign key to `form (id, document_type)`. A
version that is never edited uses `refuse_edit()` (as map versions, zones and site shapes do since 1.1.7). The
example world's P1 has a load form (Vegetative, C&D), a haul-out form and an incident form
(`world.forms`, `world.formDebrisTypes`).

**"The prime" is one key** (ADR-305): a table that names a prime (`Contract` today; a pay item's
rate in 1.1.6, a certification in 1.2.3) holds it with a two-column foreign key (project, prime) to
`project_contractor (project_id, as_prime_id)`, so only one of the project's own primes can be
named. Whoever adds a prime to a project writes `asPrimeId` = its contractor; a database test uses
`primeOn(project, contractor)` and `subOn(project, contractor, prime, tier)`
(`packages/db/test/support/example-world.ts`). A contractor's kind has no default.

**A project is written whole** (ADR-303): no setting has a database default. A story or a service
starts from `new NewProjectSettings(policy).for(programType)` (`packages/domain`), the policy read
from `packages/domain/policy.env` (a story: `story.policy`); a database test uses
`projectLike(world, …)` and `insertOf` (`packages/db/test/support/example-world.ts`). **A new
threshold** is a name in the domain's `policyNames` and a line in `policy.env`, with an ADR; never a
literal, never a database default.

**A new list** (if a task needs one) is a model in `configuration.prisma` with the six list columns,
then `SELECT guard_list('<table>', '<domain>');` in its guard migration; a new built-in key goes in
`packages/domain`'s `builtInKeys` first, with an ADR (ADR-302).

Start every command with `eval "$(fnm env --shell zsh)"`; the checks are **`adms-verify`** (the chain
is 80 files, 1,752 tests; eighty migrations; `pnpm scenarios` runs fifteen stories, 16, 18, 52, 25, 15, 35, 47, 4, 39, 28, 30, 27, 26, 27 and 25 checks),
with **`pnpm security`** (7 passed, 0 failed, ADR-291; **6 passed, 1 failed since 2026-10-05**, one new advisory on the test runner's `source-map-js`, fixed from 2026-10-07 by ADR-356's override, BACKLOG C74). The database tests, the map servers' tests and
the stories need `pnpm local:up` first; stop it at close-out (ADR-277). A schema change goes through
Prisma (`prisma migrate dev --create-only`), a guard into its own empty stub (ADR-113); **try a guard
migration on a throw-away copy before `pnpm installer` applies it**, since an applied one is never
edited. **Loosened guards are tried two at a time on this machine**, each on its own copy
(`adms_mutation_0`, `_1`; `adms-verify` §1.3; four at once filled Docker's disk on 2026-10-03): run
nothing else against the database, and no `pnpm lint` or `pnpm test`, while they go.

**Words and examples everywhere:** `spec/CONVENTIONS.md` (ADR-234, 235). Field names:
`spec/DATA-MODEL.md`. Flag wording: `spec/FLAGS.md`.

#### From ROADMAP.md §6, a row approved 2026-10-06

| **The defaults of corrections and renumbering (ADR-364)** | Seven, none changes what a monitor does. The system checks a person's permission itself each time (an admin needs none). *Renumber* covers a ticket number, a split's suffix and resolving a quarantined record; *correct* covers everything else, a record created for a failed phone included. A correction asks for no reason, only an optional note. A quarantined record is resolved one of two ways, once: renumbered, or marked a second copy. A white goods line or a carried ticket is "taken off", never deleted. A reviewer can't change what kind of record something is. And one wording: the example reason "Phone failed" isn't on the shipped list ("Device failed" is) | Tell the agent to change any of them |

#### From ROADMAP.md §6, a row approved 2026-10-06

| **The defaults of the reviewer's records (ADR-363)** | Six, none changes money. An invoice batch's name can be used once on a project. A contractor's login sees that its own tickets are locked as invoiced and in which batch, and sees no QC status, no accepted flag and no void. Nobody with a read-only login reads the note written when a ticket is unlocked. A lock once unlocked, or a void once lifted, is never changed again: locking or voiding again makes a new record, so the history shows each time. QC Void on a certification does nothing to the tickets on it. A note with an unlock or an unvoid is optional. Say if any should be otherwise | Whenever you like; the next three tasks build on them |

A void ticket can't be locked as invoiced. A ticket's QC status can't be changed while it is locked. Closing a project only marks it closed: nothing is refused on a closed project | Any time |

#### From BACKLOG.md, "Historical — Phase 1 closeout on `database/`" (Milestones H1.1…H1.3, never worked: the rebuild closed their KDs, ADR-371)

## Historical — Phase 1 closeout on `database/` *(superseded by ADR-093/103; kept as rebuild requirements)*

> Its milestones and tasks are numbered **H1.x** (relabelled 2026-10-01, ADR-300) so they are never
> taken for Phase 1's milestones 1.0…1.9 above. They belong to the historical code (ADR-093) and are
> kept as the list of behaviours and lessons the rebuild must satisfy, **not** as work to do.

### Milestone H1.1 — Baseline verification (do this first, every session on a fresh clone)
- [ ] **H1.1.1** `docker compose up -d`; confirm the Postgres healthcheck passes.
- [ ] **H1.1.2** `cd database && npm install && npm run db:migrate` — confirm all migrations apply clean.
- [ ] **H1.1.3** `cd database && npm run typecheck` — confirm zero errors.
- [ ] **H1.1.4** `cd database/python && python -m pytest tests/ -v` — confirm 71 pass. Record the
      real number; if it differs from 71, update this file and note why.
- [ ] **H1.1.5** `cd database && npm run db:seed`, then `curl http://localhost:8001/health` with the
      engine running — confirm end-to-end reconciliation produces both matched and failed tickets.

### Milestone H1.2 — Close the known deviations
Each of these is a real gap between the domain skills and the code, tracked in `agent_store/DEVIATIONS.md`.
Do **not** start one without reading its Known Deviation entry first.

- [ ] **H1.2.1** **KD-01 — reconciler writes no `Transaction`.** The engine sets tickets to
      `MATCHED` and writes `LoadTicket` / `HaulOutTicket`, but nothing ever writes the financial
      ledger row. `transactionService.createTransaction` exists and is never called from the
      reconciliation path. Decide and implement the write path (Python direct vs. Node callback),
      record the decision as an ADR, and cover it with a DB integration test.
- [ ] **H1.2.2** **KD-02 — `_validate_disposal` has an inconsistent return type.** It returns
      `list[ValidationError]` on its two early returns (`CERT_NOT_FOUND`, `SITE_NOT_FOUND`) but
      the tuple `(errors, cert)` on the normal path. `reconcile_load_pair` papers over this with an `isinstance` check. Normalise to
      a single return shape and delete the workaround.
- [ ] **H1.2.3** ⚠️ **Moot if the Q-13 status proposal is accepted** (every engine failure → review). **KD-03 — haul-out escalation set differs from the load workflow.**
      `ROUTE_DRIFT_EXCEEDED` softens to `MANUAL_REVIEW` in `reconcile_load_pair` but hard-`FAILED`s
      in `reconcile_haul_out_pair`. Confirm with the user whether this asymmetry is intended
      policy; either document it as intentional in domain-skill terms via an ADR, or unify it.
- [ ] **H1.2.4** **KD-04 — haul-out failures write no audit record.**
      `reconcile_load_pair` calls `_audit_recon_failure` for both halves; `reconcile_haul_out_pair`
      and `reconcile_unit_rate` do not. Invariant 3 says every mutation is audited. Fix.
- [ ] **H1.2.5** **KD-05 — `_audit_recon_failure` hard-codes `"FAILED"`** in its `newValue` payload
      even when the actual outcome was `MANUAL_REVIEW`, so the audit trail misreports the status.
      Pass the real status through.
- [ ] **H1.2.6** **KD-06 — orphan disposals are invisible.** The load cycle iterates collections
      only, so a `DisposalTicket` with no matching collection stays `PENDING` silently forever.
      Per the `adms-exceptions` skill §4.3 that is a fraud signal. Surface it in the `ReconcileResult` summary.

- [ ] **H1.2.7** **KD-10 — cert numbers.** ⚠️ **Reframed by ADR-045 (2026-09-24):** a supplied number
      from pre-printed certification paper is valid; uniqueness is `@@unique([projectId, certNumber])`;
      add a system issuer for when none is supplied, and don't reject supplied numbers. Text below
      predates that. Per ADR-016 the cert number
      *is* the placard number and must be issued by the system like a ticket number. Today
      `certificationService.ts` takes it as caller-supplied free text and `BaseCertification`
      has no `@unique` on it — so two certifications can share a number and the reconciler
      would happily pair tickets from two different containers. Add a `generateCertNumber()`
      in `database/src/lib/`, issue it inside both cert create paths, add the unique constraint
      via `npm run db:migrate`, and update `scripts/run_test.ts` (which currently hand-authors
      `"CERT-TRK-001"` style values). **Decide and record in an ADR:** the number format
      (short human-legible like `10090`, per the `adms-ledger-audit` skill §6.3) and whether uniqueness is
      global or per-project.
- [ ] **H1.2.8** **KD-11 — `ContainerType` cannot express real configurations.** `SELF_LOADER |
      TRAILER` does not cover a tandem dump truck, a pickup pulling a trailer, or an integral
      built-in bed (the `adms-certifications` skill §3A.1). **Blocked pending a user decision on the taxonomy** —
      do not guess at enum values. Resolve before Phase 3 builds a picker against it.

- [ ] **H1.2.9** **KD-13 → KD-12 — re-base pairing on the ticket number.** One change, in order:
      (a) make the generator emit a bare number (no `COL-`/`DIS-` prefix, no date — ADR-046) and call it **only** on the
      collection-side creates — `CollectionTicket`, `HaulOutCollectionTicket`, `UnitRateTicket`;
      (b) make `createDisposalTicket` / `createHaulOutDisposalTicket` **accept** the scanned
      number rather than generate one; (c) replace `_find_disposal_match` /
      `_find_haul_disposal_match` with grouping by `ticketNumber` over the queue; (d) keep cert /
      zone / debris / timing as **validation** on the grouped pair (§5.1), and add the explicit
      `TICKET_TYPE_MISMATCH` check that the composite match used to make implicit.
      ⚠️ **Revised by ADR-062:** the constraints change from global `@unique` to
      `@@unique([projectId, ticketNumber])` (KD-43) — still what rejects a duplicate at sync, now per
      project. Reconciled records carry the load's own number (no `LDT`/`HOT`); labels are display only.
- [ ] **H1.2.9a** **ADR-022 — quarantine rejected sync payloads.** A duplicate-number insert must
      persist the rejected record in full with its rejection reason and the id of the record
      holding the number, surface it in a review queue, and **never** acknowledge it to the device
      as saved. Silently dropping it destroys evidence of real work and permanently unbills a
      legitimate load. Needs a quarantine model — flag the schema addition before building it.
- [ ] **H1.2.10** **Duplicate and orphan shapes (the `adms-exceptions` skill §4.3a).** Cover the table at the
      end of §4.3a with tests: duplicate disposal (canonical), duplicate collection (escalate —
      an issuance defect, not a keying slip), ageing collection orphans, and disposal-with-no-
      collection (strongest fraud signal — never auto-resolve). A 3+ group in the queue should be
      unreachable under ADR-021; assert that, and if one is ever seen, route every member to
      `MANUAL_REVIEW` and bill nothing.
- [ ] **H1.2.11** ⚠️ **Widened by ADR-051:** any captured field is correctable, not only the number —
      see H1.2.21. **Reviewer ticket-number correction (ADR-020).** The one permitted post-submission
      field change. Service function, `MANUAL_REVIEW`-only, rejects `MATCHED`/billed tickets,
      writes an `AuditRecord` under the **reviewer's** user id retaining the prior number, and
      returns the affected records to `PENDING` for the next sweep. Must not be callable to edit
      any other field.
- [ ] **H1.2.12** **KD-15 — silent no-op rules.** Evaluate rules for `HAUL_OUT_DISPOSAL`. Then
      **decide** what `LOAD` / `HAUL_OUT`-targeted rules mean — run them post-pairing against the
      joined record, or reject the type at rule creation. Accepting a rule and never running it is
      not an option; add a test asserting every `TicketType` a rule may target is actually reached.
- [ ] **H1.2.13** **KD-14 — project-enabled ticket types.** Add the `Project → TicketType` relation
      per ADR-018 and the First Principles model, enforce it at ticket creation in
      `ticketService.ts`, and constrain rule authoring to the enabled set.

- [ ] **H1.2.14** **KD-16 — split the org model.** Per ADR-023/024: add `DeclarationEvent`
      (event name + flexible `declarationRef` like `DR-9001-FL` + reference type + incident
      dates), add `programType` to `Project` (`ROW | PARKS | PPDR | WATERWAY`), and derive
      `requireRoe` from `programType` instead of carrying it on `Program`. ⚠️ **This is a
      migration, not a rename** — `Project.programId` and `Transaction.programId` both reference
      `Program` today. Update `referenceDataService`, the seed, and any Python query touching
      `Program`. **Blocked on KD-17** (the enum value set). Event scoping is **settled** — per ADR-026
      `DeclarationEvent` is a shared global object, so today's FK shape (`Project.clientId` +
      `Project.programId`) is already right: `Program` becomes `DeclarationEvent`, `programType`
      moves onto `Project`.
- [ ] **H1.2.15** **KD-17 — confirm the `ProgramType` value set.** User-confirmed: `ROW`, `PARKS`,
      `PPDR`, `WATERWAY`. `CPDR` and `DEMOLITION` have reference-doc support. §3.1a now carries a
      fuller proposed set grouped by disaster context (hurricane, flood, wildfire, common,
      man-made/mass-casualty) — all still **proposals**. **Do not populate the enum unilaterally**;
      a wrong value set propagates into ROE logic, rule authoring and field-app project setup.
- [ ] ~~**H1.2.15a**~~ ⚫ **Dropped — ADR-052:** incidents never stop work; no holds. **KD-21 — stop-work holds.** ⚠️ **Do not build from the notes in §3.1a.** The
      human-remains protocol halts an *area*, not a record, and the requirements vary by
      jurisdiction, contract and event type. Get the governing protocol from the user first.
- [ ] **H1.2.16** **KD-18 — add reference-data update paths.** Per ADR-025 reference data is
      legitimately editable. `referenceDataService` has create/archive but no update, yet the
      primary flow is *select an existing client and update its contact details* (ADR-023). Add
      audited `update*` functions for `Client`, `Contractor`, `Contract`, `DisposalSite`. Keep
      soft-archive; add no delete path. Do **not** extend this to tickets or certifications.
- [ ] **H1.2.17** **Enforce ROE by program type.** ⚠️ **Revised by ADR-052/055: flag, never block.** Once
      `programType` exists, a ticket on a project that requires ROEs is **flagged for review** after
      reconcile when its ROE is missing, unsigned or out of scope. (Original: must block ticket creation against a parcel with no signed ROE.) Today
      `Program.requireRoe` is stored and never enforced anywhere in `ticketService.ts` — the same
      silent-no-op class as KD-15.

- [ ] **H1.2.18** **KD-19 (reframed) — group on the BASE ticket number.** Per ADR-032/033 splits
      are N collections → 1 disposal for PPDR/ROE work, each with a distinct suffixed number, so
      **there is no uniqueness conflict** — do not change any `@unique` constraint. The work is
      the grouping rule: strip any `-A`..`-Z` suffix to form the group key, accept N collections
      (N≥1) + exactly one disposal, require split members to share cert / debris type / zone, and
      route ambiguous shapes (two disposals on a base, suffix gaps, orphan chains) to
      `MANUAL_REVIEW`. Test a 5-member chain end to end.
- [ ] **H1.2.18a** **KD-22 / KD-23 — per-property attribution on splits.** Add
      `monitorEstimatedCy` and `roeId` to `CollectionTicket`. The estimate is an **observation**,
      so it is immutable after submission (invariant 5) — unlike apportioned tonnage. Make the
      field conditional on `programType` requiring ROEs (ADR-024) once KD-16/17 land. Then add the
      cross-check: `Σ estimates` vs `capacity × load call`, tolerance from `.env`, divergence to
      review.
- [ ] **H1.2.18b** **KD-24 — scale receipts.** ⚠️ Read §4.3a *When does a scale receipt exist at
      all?* first — most loads legitimately have none, and validating unconditionally would fail
      the majority of honest work.
      **(a) Conditionality (ADR-036):** a TDSR load never has one; an FDS load has one only if the
      contract asks. Add the scale-required flag to `PayItem` and the `SCALE_NUMBER` rule
      condition (ADR-037) — tested on a **grouped pair**, never blocking pairing, missing-when-
      required → `MANUAL_REVIEW` not `FAILED`.
      **(b) Model (ADR-034):** `ScaleReceipt` with the external number stored verbatim, unique per
      project, referenced by N disposal tickets. Name it **receipt**, not ticket — it must never
      be confusable with `ticketNumber`. Gross/tare/net optional, because many receipts carry only
      a number.
      **(c) Apportionment (ADR-035):** by load-called volume, server-side, deterministic, observed
      and derived stored separately, `Σ apportioned` equal to the net exactly. Only reachable when
      a weight actually exists.
      **(d) Cases:** cover the §4.3a table — net = 0 valid when optional and invalid when required,
      tare/gross configuration mismatch rejected rather than computed, two debris types on one
      receipt voided by default, duplicate receipt numbers (transcription, not scanning).
      Tons-per-CY factors are **configuration** — do not invent values.
- [ ] ~~**H1.2.19**~~ ⚫ **Dropped — ADR-053:** no grace period, no ageing. **KD-20 — age-based orphan detection, in field time.** Per ADR-029/030, add a
      configurable grace period computed from `loadEndTime` / `disposalStartTime` — **never from
      server `createdAt`**, which under EOD sync is an accident of which tablet found signal
      first. Surface only aged unpartnered tickets; `PENDING` is never alerted on directly.
      Threshold must tolerate a device dark for days. Keep it out of the reconciler's hot path.
- [ ] **H1.2.19a** **ADR-030 — make the reconciler safe for bursty, non-monotonic input.** EOD sync
      means the worker idles for hours then meets a full day's volume at once, and a device flat
      for two days injects old work behind newer work. Assert the engine never orders by arrival,
      never treats a late arrival as suspicious, and has no "already processed later work" reject
      path. Test with an out-of-order batch.
- [ ] **H1.2.20** **Void path for phantom tickets (ADR-028/051).** Needs a `VOID` state (status set
      pending Q-13) with a required reason, unlockable only by an audited override. Retains the record and its audit trail. Distinct from renumbering and from
      archiving. Service function, audited, reviewer-only, never reachable by the engine.

- [ ] **H1.2.21** **KD-25 / KD-26 — authorized corrections (ADR-039).** ⚠️ **KD-26 must be settled
      before any edit path ships.** (a) Add an edit-permission model to `User` — "sufficiently
      privileged" currently means nothing. (b) Add audited `update*` paths for tickets, certs,
      surveys and incidents, each capturing `priorValue` **before** the write, under the real
      human's id, never `SYSTEM`. (c) **Decide what happens when a ticket that already produced a
      `Transaction` is edited** — `Transaction` is append-only, so a compensating entry is the
      only mechanism, and nothing today links a correction to that reversal. Until (c) is
      answered, block edits on reconciled/billed tickets rather than letting ticket and ledger
      silently desynchronise. ⚠️ **ADR-051/057:** every captured field is editable; tickets lock as
      invoiced and unlock by audited action; mechanism proposal in Q-26.
- [ ] **H1.2.22** **KD-27 — itemized unit counts and unit rate sub-types (ADR-040/041).**
      (a) Add a JSONB item breakdown to `UnitRateTicket` alongside the integer `unitCount`, so
      `{paint_cans: 4, propane_tanks: 10}` is expressible. (b) Extend project enablement so
      `UNIT_RATE` carries a **sub-type set** (hangers, leaners, stumps, HHW, white goods), which
      determines the payload shape. Depends on KD-14. ⚠️ Keep `PayItem` decoupled from ticket
      types — it must **not** gain a `ticketType`; the `Rule` makes that link.
- [ ] **H1.2.23** **KD-28 — enforce `PayItem.requireUnitCount`.** The flag exists and defaults
      correctly but nothing reads it. Same silent-no-op class as KD-15 and `requireRoe` — a
      control an admin believes is active that is not. Enforce at the service boundary and in
      reconciliation; add a test asserting a count-requiring code rejects a countless ticket.
- [ ] **H1.2.24** **KD-29 — add a pound billing unit.** HHW is billed by the pound on most
      contracts and `BillingUnit` has no `LB`; `TON` is the wrong granularity for a box of paint
      cans. Small migration. Also decide whether `TBN` is doing real work or is dead weight.

#### From `NEXT.md`, "Where things stand (2026-10-09, through ADR-444)": the task-by-task record of Phase 2 so far

- **Phase 2 (API and sync) is open (ADR-376).** Its plan is `BACKLOG.md`'s eight milestones and 32
  tasks (ADR-377); tasks 2.0.1 (the opening and the plan), 2.1.1 (the threat model and the
  API's scenarios, ADR-379; docs), 2.1.2 (the API as a process, ADR-380…385), 2.1.3 (the
  boundary, ADR-387…392) and **2.1.4 (time limits and policy, ADR-394…396)** are done:
  Milestone 2.1 is complete. **Task 2.2.1 (sign-in's records, ADR-397…399) is done:** three
  tables read by the API alone, each with its own guards: `user_credential` (a person's password
  hash, authenticator secret and locked-until, apart from `user`), `session` (the SHA-256 of
  the refresh token in force) and `security_event` (copied by the database into the audit
  log's security domain). **Task 2.2.2 (passwords, ADR-402…406) is done:** the rules are
  `packages/domain`'s (`PasswordRules`: NIST SP 800-63B-4 and ASVS 5.0; 15 to 128 characters as
  policy values, never a composition rule or an age; a monitor's exempt, ADR-105); a password or
  a master passcode that is on the release's own list of 46,483 known breached passwords
  (`packages/domain/breached-passwords.txt`) is refused, with no outside service; a password is
  kept only as an Argon2id hash (19 MiB, 2 passes, 1 lane); `Passwords` in `apps/api/src/sign-in/`
  lets an admin set anybody's (**a service: its endpoint comes with 2.2.5**, when a session says
  who calls) and a back-office or outside user reset theirs by email through two endpoints
  (`POST /password-resets`, `/password-resets/completions`) with a signed code, good once for 60
  minutes, that stores nothing; mail is `nodemailer` and never required. What it leaves: BACKLOG
  C89. **Task 2.2.3 (sessions, ADR-407…411) is done:** an admin, a manager/analyst or a
  read-only viewer signs in with their email address and password (`POST /sessions`) and gets
  two `__Host-` cookies (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`): an access token good for five
  minutes and a refresh token that rotates and is good once (used twice, its session ends).
  **Every endpoint says who may call it** (`access` in the contracts), asked by `Admission`
  before the schemas read anything; a call that isn't a GET carries the session's CSRF value
  in `x-adms-csrf`. A session ends after 30 quiet minutes and 12 hours at most. Wrong tries
  are counted on `user_credential` (the domain's `SignInTries`): a wait from the 5th in a row,
  a lock at the 50th (ADR-417, the user's decision; the 10th before) until the password is set anew; each a security event, written with the
  person whose login was tried as its actor; a name nobody has writes nothing. A password an
  admin set is changed by its owner first (`passwordChangeRequired`); a new password ends the
  person's sessions; the password hash is keyed from `ADMS_TOKEN_SIGNING_SECRET`. A monitor
  and the system actor are refused. What it leaves: BACKLOG C90. **Task 2.2.4 (two-step
  sign-in, ADR-412) is done:** the second step is an authenticator app's code (RFC 6238, by
  `node:crypto`); a person who has one gets a session only with it (`POST /sessions` takes
  `code`; a right password without one answers `TWO_STEP_CODE_NEEDED`; a wrong or spent code
  is a wrong try at the login); a code is good once (`user_credential.two_step_last_step`);
  **an admin and a manager/analyst with none get a session that opens nothing but setting one
  up** (`TWO_STEP_SETUP_REQUIRED`; an endpoint is open to them only where its definition says
  `beforeTwoStepSetup`); a read-only viewer may choose one; a person sets it up by proving a
  code (`POST /two-step/setups`, `/two-step/setups/confirmations`; nothing is kept before
  that); the secret is kept sealed with a key drawn from the signing secret; an admin clears
  another person's (`POST /people/:userId/two-step-clearings`: their sessions end, a
  `TWO_STEP_CLEARED` security event). **The dev stack's accounts:** `pnpm local:accounts`
  writes an admin, a manager/analyst and a viewer with known passwords and authenticator
  secrets into this machine's installation (`--show` only shows them; it has not been run
  for real here, so the installation holds no person but the system actor). What it leaves:
  BACKLOG C91. **Task 2.2.5 (permissions on every request, and people, ADR-415) is done:**
  every `SIGNED_IN` endpoint names its `roles` and may name one `permission`; `Admission` asks
  them on each request from the database (`NOT_ALLOWED`), the rule the domain's (`Access`); an
  admin creates back-office and outside users (`POST /people`), reads one (`GET
  /people/:userId`, a monitor's phone number an admin's alone), gives and takes permissions and
  a viewer's projects (`PUT …/permissions`, `…/viewer-projects`), sets a password
  (`POST …/passwords`), ends sessions (`…/session-endings`) and archives (`…/archivings`); the
  database keeps one email address a person who signs in and the firm's last admin; **`pnpm
  installer:admin`** on the server makes the first admin and lets an admin back in (it has
  not been run for real here: the installation still holds no person but the system actor).
  What it leaves: BACKLOG C92. **Task 2.2.6 (rate limits, ADR-416) is done:** a caller over
  a limit is answered 429 `LIMITED` with `Retry-After` (and `retryAfterSeconds` in the body);
  every request is counted by address and, signed in, by person; refused tries at a secret by
  address and by address at one login (four, under the login's own wait: the fifth from one
  address never reaches the login); resets by email by who asks and who is asked for; nine
  policy values; the counts in the API's own memory (gone at a restart, per process), never
  the database; a caller's address taken from a proxy only where `ADMS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` lists
  it (the local stack's Caddy is `172.30.213.2` on a network of fixed addresses); no address
  logged or stored. **The user confirmed its defaults and put the lock at fifty wrong tries
  (ADR-417).** What it leaves: BACKLOG C93. **Milestone 2.2 is complete.** **Task 2.3.1 (the job queue, ADR-418) is done:** two guarded tables of our own
  written through Prisma, `reconciliation_job` and `reconciliation_job_ticket`, and no queue
  library; a job names its project, what asked for it and who, and its tickets (workflow and
  bare number); **it is added only inside the piece of work of the change that asks for it**,
  by `new ReconciliationJobs(tx).queue(…)` in `packages/db`; the API adds a job and changes
  nothing of it, the worker writes only how it went (`attempts`, `finishedAt` with its run,
  `lastError`, `setAsideAt`), nobody deletes, no viewer reads; a job once finished or set aside
  never changes. What it leaves: BACKLOG C94. **Task 2.3.2 (the worker as a process, ADR-419) is
  done:** `apps/worker/src/main.ts`, the stack's eighth service (profile `worker`), looks at the
  queue every five seconds and hands each project with a job waiting to
  `Reconciliation.waitingJobs`: under the project's lock a try is counted on each waiting job,
  the tickets they name are worked and no other, each once, and each job is finished in the
  run's closing piece of work; a try that fails whole keeps its reason, and a job is set aside
  after five (`JOB_TRIES_BEFORE_SET_ASIDE`). Its settings stop the start when off, named; its
  log is JSON by ids; its health answer (`{"status":"ok","jobsWaiting":N,"jobsSetAside":N}`) is
